fields.Name: ORD-27 - Create Order In State
fields.Description: Orders.CreateOrderInState (CS1-CS12) - back-office entry of something that has ALREADY happened: a counter sale, a shipment that went out before anyone opened the system, a migration. The check that carries the bundle is CS2. The tempting implementation is a single UPDATE setting Status='Fulfilled'; it is faster, it passes any assertion that reads the order's own fields, and it produces an order that looks complete with no ledger behind it - the failure nothing downstream can detect, because the order reconciles perfectly against itself and the revenue simply never existed. CS2 asserts the journal entries really exist and really balance, which is why this operation delegates to the real Orders.ConfirmOrder rather than writing a status.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: An order is created directly into Confirmed and the status sticks; it BOOKED, with balanced journal entries that really exist rather than a status written over an empty ledger; Posted is reached and books exactly once, so advancing past the lock does not count revenue twice; reaching Fulfilled marks the fulfillable LINES and not merely the header, so the queue cannot keep offering work the order claims to have done; an order whose product type requires no fulfilment reaches Fulfilled anyway rather than stranding every service and subscription sale; the transition trail records each step so a bulk import shows where an order stopped; Draft and Quoted are refused because routing them here would book an order not meant to be locked, and Voided is refused because voiding is a decision about an existing order; a failing confirm creates nothing and passes its own blockers through rather than replacing them with a generic failure; ExpectedGrossTotal still guards against a migration silently repricing at today's rates; a back-dated order carries the stated date; and advancing to Fulfilled writes no additional journal entry.
